failures.criterion: At 1x the head refuses nothing, reads or writes (the architect's round-9 check 1)
failures.evidence: Three adjacent 1x pairs (--events 4 --sessions 400 --requests 60): head t9-head-1x-a 0/0, t9-head-1x-b 0/0, t9-head-1x-c 126 reads (1.17%) and 8 writes (1.11%), all 429 OVERLOADED; base t9-base-1x-a 221 reads and 28 writes, t9-base-1x-b 0/0, t9-base-1x-c 0/1. t9-head-1x-c's in-window refusals fall at 10:27:58-10:28:13 (read refusal counter 38 -> 108 between the 10:27:58 and 10:28:03 samples, write 5 -> 12; loadgen logs write refusals at 10:28:09-13). In that window: no 'event horizon held back' line in Dispatch's log (none in the run); the 1 s /proc/stat sampler's ticks were 1.02-1.43 s at 50-82% CPU (no box-wide stall); Postgres's log shows 1.04 s, 2.02 s and 1.58 s executions of the artifact-listing select (stmtcache_731df244...) at 10:28:00-08 on dispatch-requests, and a dispatch-settlements backend's 'select closed_at is null from issues where key = $1 for no key update' taking 3.26 s at 10:28:09 (a row-lock wait); 33 comment writes and 27 issue reads took over 2 s each between 10:28:00 and 10:28:16. loadgen's own 5 s sampler took no sample between 10:28:03 and 10:28:16, so admission's in-flight gauges at the peak are unsampled (the 10:28:03 sample shows 15 reads and 8 writes in flight). So the burst is Postgres-side slowness (a row-lock wait and slow listing reads) filling slots for about 10 s, not the event-horizon hold of round 8 and not a box stall; which write held the issue row is not established. No red test: it appears in one of three 180 s load runs. Evidence: dispatch://INFRA-592/artifact/infra-592-tester-r9-t9-head-1x-c-tar-gz (dispatch.log, samples.json, boxcpu) and the Postgres log lines quoted here.
